# refactor(domain): assign error ownership by meaning

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**:
everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to
any other issue or pull request.

Lands after two earlier issues and builds on both: the one that splits config I/O from config
policy, and the one that moves `messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` into `src/failures/`.
Check that `src/failures/` exists before you start; if it does not, stop and say so.

## What

Every kind of failure jig reports has a clear owner. Users see the same error messages, and the
same failures are retried, blocked or fatal.

## Why

All failures live in one domain file. Business code therefore appears to depend on storage, Git and
configuration details, and each new failure type adds to a single global list.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `failures` (failure presentation, unwrapping and retry execution),
`ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and policy), `flow`/`steps`
(workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting), `adapters` (Git, files,
containers, terminal, logging), `integrations/github`, `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

Read these sections of `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`: "Target responsibilities" and "Error
ownership and technical failure handling". Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow the spec
and say so in the PR.

## Target

`src/domain/errors.ts` holds the `JigError` union, `FailureKind`, `isTransient`, `isJigError` and
21 error classes. Move each class to the owner of the condition it describes, split
`ConfigInvalid` by meaning, and replace `JigError` with narrow contracts. Do the two required first
steps below before moving any class.

**Out of scope:** `messageOf`, `rootCause`, `retryResult` and `RetryPolicy`. They already live in
`src/failures/`; import them from there and do not move, wrap or inject them.
`src/integrations/github/errors.ts` holds GitHub-specific errors; leave them for the GitHub issue
unless a shared class is involved.

### Step 1 (required first): find every place an error tag is read, shown or stored

Each class split out of `ConfigInvalid` gets its own tag (see `ConfigInvalid` below). Before
changing any tag, grep `src/` for every read of `_tag`, every match on the string `'ConfigInvalid'`,
every `instanceof` or class-name check, and every place an error is serialized or logged. For each
one, decide whether a tag change there is visible to users or breaks stored data, and put the list
in the PR. An earlier read-only investigation found the following; confirm it against the code as
it stands, since lines may have moved.

Production code that reads a jig error tag. None of these involve `ConfigInvalid`, so the split
does not affect them:

- `src/adapters/git/remote-ref.ts:57` retries when `_tag === 'RemoteUnavailable'`.
- `src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:137,140` retries and recovers on
  `_tag === 'RunStateConflict'`.
- `src/integrations/github/octokit-github.ts:62` and `implement-issue.ts:473` match GitHub's own
  tags (`GithubUnavailable`, `GithubRefused`).
- `src/config/presets.ts:51` switches on `PresetSourceFailure` tags.
- `src/adapters/sandcastle/sandcastle-session.ts:311-320` reads sandcastle's own failure tags to
  decide between `ConfigInvalid` and `SandboxUnavailable`. That tag set belongs to the library.
  The class it produces changes; nothing reads jig's tag there.

No production code compares against the string `'ConfigInvalid'` or uses
`instanceof ConfigInvalid`. Classification uses `kind` (`src/flow/engine.ts:226`), not the tag.

Surfaces that show or store errors:

| Surface | What it carries | Tag change visible or breaking? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI output and exit code (`src/cli/with-error-handling.ts:22`) | an `Err`'s `message` only; every `Err` exits 1 | No |
| Saved run state, local and remote (`blockedReason`, `src/flow/engine.ts:227`) | the error's `message` | No |
| Run events and metrics log (`reason` in `src/domain/events.ts`, `src/observers/metrics.ts:27,86`) | the error's `message` | No |
| GitHub orchestration state and comments (`src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:159`) | statuses and receipts, no errors | No |
| Telemetry (`src/observers/tracing-observer.ts:31,81`) | span status message from `reason` | No |
| Logs written with `{ err }` (`src/app/report-cleanup.ts:12`, `src/app/observed-events.ts:13`, `src/app/throwaway-sandbox.ts:61`, `src/adapters/sandcastle/sandcastle-session.ts:342,370`) | pino's error serializer writes `type` (the constructor name), `message`, `stack` and own fields, including `_tag`; `TaggedError` also sets `name` to the tag, so the stack starts with it | Visible in the console and the run's JSON log file, but only as diagnostics: nothing in jig parses them, and `type` changes with the class anyway |
| Specs | 56 `toBeInstanceOf(ConfigInvalid)` assertions across 22 spec files; `src/domain/errors.spec.ts:105` asserts `_tag === constructor.name` for every class | Instance assertions must name the new classes. The tag-equals-class-name test already requires distinct tags; keep it and extend it to the new classes |

Conclusion of that investigation: **no surface needs a compatibility translation.** Log lines show
the new tags, and that change is accepted. If you find a surface that shows the tag to users as
part of a stable output, or stores it in data that jig reads back, keep compatibility at that one
point with an explicit translation from the new tag to `'ConfigInvalid'`, and name it in the PR.

### Step 2 (required early): move retry-policy assembly from domain to flow

Retry counts and delays are technical policy, not business rules. Step retry has three owners:

- Config owns the defaults: `STEP_RETRIES = 2` and `STEP_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5000` in
  `src/config/load-config.ts`, copied by `runSettingsFrom` into `RunSettings.maxStepRetries` and
  `retryDelayMs`. Leave them there. Domain keeps the resolved `RunSettings` type.
- Classification stays with the errors: each class keeps its literal `kind`, and domain keeps
  `FailureKind` and `isTransient` as a plain rule (see "Classification" below).
- Flow owns assembling the `RetryPolicy`, because flow makes the step retry decision.

Today `transientRetryPolicy(settings: RunSettings)` returns
`{ retries: settings.maxStepRetries, delayMs: settings.retryDelayMs, shouldRetry: isTransient }`,
and its consumers are `src/flow/engine.ts` and `src/app/container.ts`. The earlier helper move may
have left it in `src/domain/retry.ts` with a structural result type that copies `RetryPolicy`'s
shape so domain need not import `failures`. Check where `transientRetryPolicy` and its result type
live when you start, and move them from there:

- Put the builder in flow, for example `src/flow/retry-policy.ts`. It imports `RetryPolicy` from
  `src/failures/retry.ts` and returns that type, not a lookalike.
- `src/flow/engine.ts` imports it from flow. `src/app/container.ts` imports it from flow too; the
  owner table allows app to import flow.
- Remove the builder and the structural lookalike type from domain. Delete `src/domain/retry.ts`
  if nothing is left in it.
- Move its specs with it. Same retries, same delays, same retryable kinds. No new settings.

### Proposed owners — verify each against its callers

A starting proposal from an earlier inventory. Every class in this table keeps its tag, message
and literal `kind`; only the classes split out of `ConfigInvalid` below get new tags. Check each row against the actual constructors and consumers; where a caller shows a
different meaning, follow the caller and record why in the PR.

| Error | Owner | Extra fields | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AgentRunFailed` | `ports/agent-session` | — | retry |
| `AgentOutputInvalid` | `ports/agent-session` | — | retry |
| `PlanNotCovered` | `domain/errors` | — | retry |
| `DesignUnresolved` | `domain/errors` | `findingIds` | block |
| `RemoteUnavailable` | `ports/git` | — | retry |
| `SandboxUnavailable` | `ports/sandbox-session` | — | retry |
| `SetupCommandFailed` | `ports/sandbox-session` | `output` | retry |
| `RunStateConflict` | `ports/run-state-failures` | — | block |
| `RunCodeUnavailable` | `ports/run-code` | — | block |
| `MergeFailed` | `ports/workspace` | — | block |
| `GitCommandFailed` | `ports/git` | `command`, `output` | block |
| `CommitImportRefused` | `ports/workspace` | — | block |
| `CommitRejected` | `ports/workspace` | `output` | block |
| `ConfigInvalid` | `config/errors`, split below | — | fatal |
| `RunRequestInvalid` | `app/run-request` | — | fatal |
| `RunInProgress` | `ports/run-lock` | — | fatal |
| `MetricsLogCorrupt` | `ports/metrics-log` | — | fatal |
| `LocalStateUnwritable` | `ports/local-state` | `path` | fatal |
| `CodexLoginNotSaved` | `ports/sandbox-session` | — | fatal |
| `ImageBuildFailed` | `ports/sandbox-images` | `output` | fatal |
| `CommandInputInvalid` | `cli/errors` | — | fatal |

Shared Git failures live once in `ports/git.ts`. Shared run-state failures live in
`ports/run-state-failures.ts`, which `run-store` and `run-code` both import, so neither imports the
other. No ports-wide error barrel and no re-exports from `domain`.

### `ConfigInvalid`

`ConfigInvalid` appears in `RunStoreFailure` (`src/ports/run-store.ts`), so moving it into config
unchanged would make ports depend on config. Keep `ConfigInvalid` in config for schema,
environment, preset and provider-selection validation only. Proposed splits for its other uses:

| Meaning today | Replacement and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid local or remote saved run; invalid state from a custom store | `RunStateInvalid`, `ports/run-state-failures` |
| Custom-store operational failure | `RunStoreOperationFailed`, `ports/run-store` |
| Loading or validating a custom-store module | `RunStoreSetupInvalid`, `app/run-stores` |
| Missing credentials, invalid selected login, credential-file access | `SandboxCredentialsInvalid`, `ports/sandbox-session` |
| Sandbox setup prerequisites or recipe validation | `SandboxPreparationInvalid`, `ports/sandbox-session` |
| Repository, root or branch prerequisites | `RepositoryInvalid`, `ports/git` |
| Symlink refusal and prerequisite file operations outside config sources | `LocalPreparationFailed`, `ports/local-state` |

Each replacement gets its own `_tag`, equal to its class name (`RunStateInvalid`,
`RunStoreOperationFailed`, and so on), so no two classes share a tag and a tag can be matched
exhaustively. Each keeps the message-only payload, the same message text and `kind: 'fatal'`, so
users see the same output and exit code. Use step 1's list for the tag checks, `instanceof`,
class-name checks and serialization to update; add a compatibility translation only where step 1
says one is needed. Keep the prerequisite cases that are deliberately
translated into `MergeFailed`. Config keeps its current import allowlist; adapters translate config
validation into capability failures where needed.

### Classification and workflow contracts

- Classes keep their literal `kind`. Domain keeps `FailureKind` and `isTransient`, which takes the
  structural input `{ kind: FailureKind }` instead of `JigError`. The flow retry-policy builder from
  step 2 uses it as `shouldRetry`.
- Replace `JigError` in `src/flow/define-flow.ts` and `src/flow/engine.ts` with step failures built
  from domain and port failures, plus each engine method's persistence failures. Flow must not
  import `steps` or `app` to derive these types (lint rule `flow-does-not-assemble-workflows`).
  `app` checks that the assembled workflow fits flow's contracts.
- Remove `JigError`. Define an aggregate only at an application operation that needs one, and keep
  CLI-only errors out of it.
- Delete `isJigError` and its class registry; nothing in production uses them.

## Don't undo these

- **`messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` stay in `src/failures/` as direct imports.** Do not
  add ports, adapters or injection for them. The same applies to the flow retry-policy builder: it
  is an ordinary function that engine and app import, not a port or a dependency passed in.
- Do not change construction or wiring in `src/app/container.ts` beyond import paths and types.
  The construction mechanism is decided separately.
- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged. The one tag change is the distinct tags of the
  classes split out of `ConfigInvalid`; their messages and exit codes stay the same.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- Change only what this issue needs. Leave unrelated specs and assertions as they are.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.

## Documentation

Internal-only work: no public guide changes. Update these references in place, present tense:
`docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
`.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md` (the paragraph about where classes live today, which also says
the move "keeps every tag": say instead that split classes get their own tags), and any other file
that names a moved path or `transientRetryPolicy`.

## Verification

From the repository root, with Node 26.13.0:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub.

## Done when

- [ ] The PR has a table with every error's old owner, new owner, and how its tag, fields and
      retry/block/fatal classification are kept at its consumers.
- [ ] `git grep -n -w -e JigError -e isJigError src` finds nothing.
- [ ] No two error classes share a `_tag`: every class's tag equals its class name, as
      `src/domain/errors.spec.ts` (or wherever its cases move) checks for every class, the new
      ones included.
- [ ] The PR lists step 1's tag read/show/store places and says which, if any, needed a
      compatibility translation.
- [ ] Domain exports no retry-policy builder and no retry-policy type:
      `git grep -n -E "export .*(RetryPolicy|transientRetryPolicy)" src/domain` finds nothing.
- [ ] The flow builder returns `RetryPolicy` imported from `src/failures/retry.ts`, and
      `src/flow/engine.ts` and `src/app/container.ts` import the builder from flow.
- [ ] Domain imports no capability, config or CLI error. Ports import nothing outside domain and
      ports (`npm run lint:dependencies`).
- [ ] Behavior tests show unchanged classification and messages, including retries running out and
      becoming blocked with the same count and delays, immediate blocking, fatal propagation,
      malformed saved state and original-cause reporting.
- [ ] The verification above passes.



Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/56

docs.design:
# Design

## Goal

Assign each failure to the module that owns its meaning, remove the global `JigError` contract and registry, and move step retry-policy assembly into flow. Preserve messages, payloads, classifications, retry timing, blocking, fatal propagation and exit codes. Classes split from `ConfigInvalid` receive distinct class-name tags.

## Context

The prerequisite is satisfied: `src/failures/messages.ts` and `src/failures/retry.ts` exist. The latter exports generic `RetryPolicy<E>` and implements immediate first attempts followed by exponential delays. These helpers remain unchanged and directly imported.

Today `src/domain/errors.ts` defines all 21 classes, `FailureKind`, `isTransient`, `JigError` and the `isJigError` registry. This hides capability and configuration dependencies inside domain. `src/domain/retry.ts` assembles settings into `TransientRetryPolicy`, duplicating the shape of the real retry contract. Engine and container consume that builder.

Config owns retry defaults and `runSettingsFrom`; domain owns resolved `RunSettings`. Flow owns execution and classification decisions, but `define-flow.ts` and `engine.ts` currently accept the global union. `RunStoreFailure` includes `ConfigInvalid`, preventing a simple relocation into config. Custom-store loading and execution in `app/run-stores.ts` also conflate module setup, operational failures and invalid returned state.

The house rules require semantic ownership, narrow `Result` failures, adapter translation of external exceptions, parsing at edges and no new throws. Dependency enforcement resides in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with fixture specs. Ports may import domain and ports; flow cannot import app or steps; config retains its existing allowlist. The architecture map describes current imports, including composition still living in app.

The inspected production tag checks concern remote availability, run-state conflicts, GitHub failures, preset-source failures and sandcastle library failures. Planning checks `PlanNotCovered`; sandbox initialization checks `SetupCommandFailed`. Config-source checks and ordinary library/error checks also exist. None requires recognizing the old `ConfigInvalid` class at runtime. Classification in the engine uses `kind`.

Error presentation has two distinct paths: CLI, saved blocked reasons, events, metrics and telemetry carry messages; Pino diagnostics serialize error identity as well. Diagnostic call sites include `report-cleanup`, `observed-events`, `throwaway-sandbox`, container's sandbox retry callback and sandbox-session cleanup, including login-release cleanup.

## Chosen approach

Complete the read/show/store audit first, then move the retry builder and its specs before relocating any class. The builder becomes `src/flow/retry-policy.ts`, returning the imported `RetryPolicy<{ kind: FailureKind }>` rather than a structural copy. `isTransient` accepts that structural classification input. Engine and container import the ordinary function from flow; domain's retry module disappears. Defaults, callbacks and retry execution remain unchanged.

Move classes together with their constructors, consumers, failure signatures and relevant tests. Do not introduce re-exports or a ports-wide error barrel. The ownership inventory is:

| Existing class, currently in domain/errors | New owner | Preserved contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AgentRunFailed | ports/agent-session | Same tag and message; retry |
| AgentOutputInvalid | ports/agent-session | Same tag and message; retry |
| PlanNotCovered | domain/errors | Same tag and message; retry |
| DesignUnresolved | domain/errors | Same tag, message and findingIds; block |
| RemoteUnavailable | ports/git | Same tag and message; retry |
| SandboxUnavailable | ports/sandbox-session | Same tag and message; retry |
| SetupCommandFailed | ports/sandbox-session | Same tag, message and output; retry |
| RunStateConflict | ports/run-state-failures | Same tag and message; block |
| RunCodeUnavailable | ports/run-code | Same tag and message; block |
| MergeFailed | ports/workspace | Same tag and message; block |
| GitCommandFailed | ports/git | Same tag, message, command and output; block |
| CommitImportRefused | ports/workspace | Same tag and message; block |
| CommitRejected | ports/workspace | Same tag, message and output; block |
| ConfigInvalid | config/errors and meaning-specific replacements below | Configuration retains its tag; replacements have distinct tags; all retain message and fatal kind |
| RunRequestInvalid | app/run-request | Same tag and message; fatal |
| RunInProgress | ports/run-lock | Same tag and message; fatal |
| MetricsLogCorrupt | ports/metrics-log | Same tag and message; fatal |
| LocalStateUnwritable | ports/local-state | Same tag, message and path; fatal |
| CodexLoginNotSaved | ports/sandbox-session | Same tag and message; fatal |
| ImageBuildFailed | ports/sandbox-images | Same tag, message and output; fatal |
| CommandInputInvalid | cli/errors | Same tag and message; fatal |

Split `ConfigInvalid` by the condition at each construction site:

| Meaning | Class and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Configuration-source, schema, environment, preset and provider-selection validation | ConfigInvalid in config/errors |
| Invalid local, remote or custom-store saved state | RunStateInvalid in ports/run-state-failures |
| Custom-store operational failure | RunStoreOperationFailed in ports/run-store |
| Custom-store module loading or validation | RunStoreSetupInvalid in app/run-stores |
| Credentials, selected login and credential-file access | SandboxCredentialsInvalid in ports/sandbox-session |
| Sandbox prerequisites and recipe validation | SandboxPreparationInvalid in ports/sandbox-session |
| Repository root and branch prerequisites | RepositoryInvalid in ports/git |
| Symlink refusal and prerequisite file operations outside configuration sources | LocalPreparationFailed in ports/local-state |

Each replacement has only the existing message payload and literal fatal kind. Preserve existing configuration-source error handling: configuration read/write and parse failures still become configuration validation failures at their current boundary. Keep existing `LocalStateUnwritable` cases and deliberate prerequisite-to-`MergeFailed` translations. Where sandbox adapters consume config policy, translate validation into the capability failure promised to callers without changing the message. Shared state failures live below both run-store and run-code; neither port imports the other merely to obtain `RunStateConflict`.

Define flow-owned step failure unions using only domain and port contracts, reflecting the actual run-step and slice-step operations. Engine methods add only persistence failures they can return; methods that consume retry/block failures expose the remaining fatal and persistence failures. App's workflow assembly checks assignability to those contracts. Narrow remaining application, CLI wrapper and GitHub orchestration signatures at their own boundaries. An application operation may define its necessary aggregate, excluding CLI input errors. Do not substitute `Error`, `unknown`, or another universal union for `JigError`.

There is one explicit request/spec mismatch. The request accepts changed diagnostic tags, but the specification requires translation wherever a surface shows or stores the old tag. Following the required spec precedence, preserve legacy diagnostic identity at the logging serialization boundary. Use Pino's existing error serializer and a thin adapter-local translation of split-error serialized identity to `ConfigInvalid`, including `_tag`, `type`, any serialized `name`, and the stack's error-name prefix. Do not mutate error instances, rewrite message contents or stack frames, or change original-cause reporting. Keep runtime tags distinct and unrelated errors untouched. Apply this to console and run-file logger construction, leaving container wiring unchanged. The mapping is a diagnostic compatibility mapping, not a recognition registry; it must not import application classes into adapters. Record this deliberate deviation in the PR.

No compatibility translation is needed for message-only CLI output, saved state, events, metrics or telemetry. Audit any additional serialization surface before concluding the inventory. Existing GitHub-specific classes remain where they are.

## Alternatives considered

1. Move all classes to a central failures module or re-export them from domain. Rejected because technical helpers would become a global semantic registry, and dependency ownership would remain hidden.
2. Move `ConfigInvalid` unchanged or preserve its tag in every replacement. Rejected because ports would depend on config, unrelated conditions would remain conflated, and duplicate tags would prevent exhaustive discrimination.
3. Allow diagnostic tags to change without translation. This is simpler and explicitly accepted by the issue, but rejected because the supplied specification takes precedence and explicitly preserves tags at showing/storing surfaces. Translation remains confined to diagnostics.

## Assumptions

- The checked-in application-boundaries specification governs disagreements; diagnostic compatibility is the identified disagreement.
- Current caller meanings support the proposed owners. Any constructor-specific deviation discovered during the complete inventory must be documented with its consumer rationale.
- Existing malformed-state handling, configuration-source translation, cleanup precedence and original-cause behavior are contracts to preserve.
- Node 26.13.0 is the verification runtime. This design task performs no implementation or verification run.

## Non-goals

No composition extraction, container construction changes, GitHub-specific error redistribution, generic workflow framework, new settings, retry helper changes, injected failure utilities, public command changes, release tags or version bumps. No host agent execution, publication, credential persistence changes or writes to target-repository tracked files outside the existing authorized paths.

## Affected areas

Domain error and retry modules; owning port modules; config/errors; app/run-request and app/run-stores; CLI errors and wrappers; flow contracts and engine; app workflow assembly and container imports/types; constructing adapters and consuming steps, observers and GitHub orchestration; logging serialization; colocated specs and necessary dependency fixtures.

Update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`, plus existing references to moved paths and the retry builder. Describe current ownership in present tense and explicitly state that split classes receive distinct tags. Public guides need no behavioral changes.

# Implementation plan

## Step 1 — Complete the ownership and compatibility inventory

Confirm `src/failures/` exists before implementation; stop if absent. Read the applicable rules, architecture map and specified application-boundaries sections. Inventory every class constructor, consumer and failure signature.

Search all `src/`, including specs, for `_tag`, `ConfigInvalid` string matches, `instanceof`, class/name checks and error logging or serialization. Trace values to outputs rather than treating every JSON serialization as error persistence. Record exact paths and locations for:

- Remote-ref retry, orchestration-store conflict handling, GitHub tag matches, preset-source matching and sandcastle's library-tag extraction.
- Planning and sandbox setup class checks, config-source checks, generic Error/library checks and the removable registry.
- CLI message/exit handling, saved blocked reasons, events, metrics, telemetry, local/remote state and GitHub receipts/comments.
- Cleanup logging in report-cleanup, observed-events, throwaway-sandbox and sandcastle-session, plus container's sandbox retry logging and both logger factories.
- Spec assertions on old classes, tags, fields and classification.

Prepare the PR's complete old/new ownership table and read/show/store table. Record that the spec requires diagnostic compatibility despite the issue accepting changed logs. Finish this audit before changing tags; no classes move yet.

## Step 2 — Move retry-policy assembly into flow

Move `transientRetryPolicy` and its colocated specs to `src/flow/retry-policy.ts` and `.spec.ts`. Return the existing imported `RetryPolicy<{ kind: FailureKind }>` and change `isTransient` to accept `{ kind: FailureKind }`. Update engine and container imports, remove `TransientRetryPolicy`, and delete the empty domain retry module.

Preserve resolved settings, config defaults, caller callbacks and exponential-delay execution. Verify builder behavior for retry, block and fatal inputs and unchanged settings propagation. Finish this step before relocating classes.

## Step 3 — Relocate unchanged classes with their consumers

Move all classes whose meanings do not require splitting to their designated owners. Keep `PlanNotCovered`, `DesignUnresolved`, `FailureKind` and `isTransient` in domain. Introduce shared Git and run-state failure modules without barrels or domain re-exports.

Update constructors, port contracts, imports and affected specs together. Preserve literal kinds, tags, message construction and additional fields. Update planning's class checks and sandbox setup's `SetupCommandFailed` checks. Existing GitHub classes stay in place; only imports of shared classes change.

Keep the transitional union only as long as needed for the following contract changes; do not expose it as a new supported boundary.

## Step 4 — Split ConfigInvalid and preserve diagnostic compatibility

Move configuration validation to `config/errors.ts`. Replace other construction sites by meaning with `RunStateInvalid`, `RunStoreOperationFailed`, `RunStoreSetupInvalid`, `SandboxCredentialsInvalid`, `SandboxPreparationInvalid`, `RepositoryInvalid` and `LocalPreparationFailed`.

Update local/remote saved-state parsing and the custom-store wrapper together with `RunStoreFailure`. Separate custom-module setup from operation failure and invalid returned state. Update credential handling, provider/config-to-sandbox translations, image recipes, repository prerequisites and non-config prerequisite file operations with their callers and specs. Preserve existing `MergeFailed` conversions and `LocalStateUnwritable` cases.

Implement diagnostic compatibility in the logging adapter using Pino's serializer, shared by console and run-file logger creation. Translate only split-class serialized identity to the legacy ConfigInvalid identity, without mutating errors or importing app classes. Preserve original messages and stack bodies. Add focused tests covering serialized identity, unchanged runtime tags, unchanged unrelated errors and both logging destinations. Document this spec-over-request decision in the PR inventory.

Verify representative malformed saved-state, custom-store setup/operation, credential, preparation, repository and local-file failures retain their exact existing messages and fatal classification. Do not broaden config's dependency allowlist.

## Step 5 — Replace global failure contracts and remove the registry

Inventory the actual failure sets of run and slice steps. Define flow-owned unions from domain/port classes and capability contracts. Update `RunStep`, `SliceStep` and engine method signatures, distinguishing returned fatal step failures from consumed retry/block failures and adding each method's persistence failures.

Check assembled workflows against these contracts in app without flow importing steps or app. Narrow application operations, CLI wrappers and GitHub orchestration where they still reference `JigError`; retain generic message-only presentation where already appropriate. Remove `JigError`, `isJigError` and the class registry completely.

Preserve cross-class tag/class-name and uniqueness coverage in a test location permitted to import the owners, rather than recreating a production registry or introducing outward imports into domain specs. Keep owner-local field and classification coverage. Extend only the existing dependency checker and fixture suite if new contract placement needs enforcement coverage.

## Step 6 — Verify workflow behavior and update ownership references

Update existing behavior specs alongside the refactor and fill genuine gaps for retry exhaustion, attempt callbacks including the final failure, unchanged exponential delays, immediate blocking, fatal propagation, persistence failures, malformed saved state, cleanup precedence and original-cause reporting. Use port fakes and existing temporary-repository helpers; real agents and sandcastle stay out of the unit suite.

Update architecture.html, workflow-ownership.md, CONTRIBUTING.md's code map and errors-as-values.md in place. Remove stale global-error and domain-retry examples, describe flow's retry builder, and document distinct split-class tags plus diagnostic compatibility. Search other references to moved paths and `transientRetryPolicy`; update affected references without adding a change-history guide.

Complete the PR tables with final constructor/consumer evidence, unchanged fields and kinds, new split tags, all audited surfaces and the sole diagnostic translation boundary.

## Step 7 — Run required verification and review the final diff

Use Node 26.13.0. Inspect verification scripts before execution to confirm none starts an agent on the host or publishes to GitHub. Run from the repository root:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

Run the required absence checks; no matches are expected:

```sh
git grep -n -w -e JigError -e isJigError src
git grep -n -E 'export .*(RetryPolicy|transientRetryPolicy)' src/domain
```

Confirm engine and container import the builder from flow and its return type comes directly from failures/retry. Confirm domain has no outward error imports, ports import only domain/ports, config's allowlist is unchanged, and container edits are limited to imports and types. Review unique tags, compatibility serialization, untouched helper implementation, unchanged messages and classification, documentation accuracy and scope. Fix failures and rerun affected checks; record actual verification results and any remaining blocker without claiming unexecuted checks passed.
